A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OrderChain, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and references supporting reliable comparison. Neither contains an appendix or the separate Supplemental Document mentioned in Section 4.1; that external material cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v2 reports original OrderChain experiments on four ordinal-regression datasets and component ablations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds zero-shot transfer results in Table 6 and case-level predictions in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The task-aware prompts, recursive category division and iterative RO-CoT procedure remain unchanged. Section 3.2 and Figure 3 clarify the existing workflow without establishing a new component or altered algorithm.

E1.justification: Section 4.4 adds evaluation on APTOS for retinopathy grading, reported AVA aesthetic assessment and KonIQ image quality assessment. This substantially extends coverage to unseen datasets and a new task domain. The precise AVA identity is unclear because its reference describes action videos.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every retained benchmark and ablation table, including the renumbered aesthetics and retinopathy tables. Table 6 reuses baseline LLaVA without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 adds an inference-only transfer evaluation on additional in-domain and out-of-domain datasets using accuracy and MAE. Previously reported training settings and split references remain unchanged; detailed splits and label construction for the new evaluation are not supplied.

E4.justification: The new generalization study tests whether ordinal understanding transfers beyond the training datasets, substantially extending analysis beyond the retained component ablations. Figure 6 also adds three people-aesthetics cases, including an overprediction, to examine the existing positive-bias hypothesis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. The additional results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the five retained tables are unchanged after matching Tables 3 and 4 across renumbering. New Table 6 reports baseline versus OrderChain accuracy of 23.2 versus 70.0 on APTOS, 49.6 versus 57.7 on AVA, and 36.3 versus 51.5 on KonIQ; corresponding MAEs are 1.02 versus 0.30, 0.56 versus 0.44, and 0.81 versus 0.49. These are newly reported transfer results, not improvements over v2 under retained settings.

T1.justification: The ordered-category formulation and recursive-division equations (1)–(4) are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The conclusion newly claims considerable zero-shot generalization performance. The abstract's principal performance claims and the introduction's novelty and unified ordinal-understanding contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 removes the explicit warning that unseen-domain zero-shot performance may suffer and the associated few-shot adaptation discussion. It adds interpretations of transfer results, attributes APTOS performance to related-task training, and states the existing people-bias and DR imbalance explanations more firmly. The aesthetic-subjectivity limitation remains in Section 4.2.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a project-page link, providing new access information without establishing what resources are available there. Section 4.1 retains the same hardware, backbone, LoRA, optimizer, learning rate, batch size and referral to a separate Supplemental Document.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for APTOS, KonIQ-10k and AVA to accompany the transfer study. The AVA reference concerns action videos despite the aesthetic-assessment description. The substantive related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain stable.

P1.justification: v3 condenses the introduction's component descriptions, rephrases RO-CoT instructions and swaps the DR and aesthetics discussion order. It removes the standalone limitations section, adds a generalization subsection and acknowledgements, and revises affiliations; most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is substantially redesigned to display the iterative workflow explicitly. Figure 4 becomes a single-column display, Figure 5 adds an input image and ground-truth label and revises prompt colors, and Figure 6 and Table 6 are new. Multiple retained tables are relocated, substantially changing the visual organization.

improvement.justification: Section 4.4 and Table 6 partially address v2's lack of empirical support for transfer to unseen datasets, while the redesigned Figure 3 clarifies the procedure. These provide a modest overall gain. Sparse new evaluation details, the AVA citation mismatch, removal of the explicit unseen-domain caveat and stronger causal language limit that gain; the core method and established benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
